0.long_answer: Bevacizumab is a monoclonal antibody that targets vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). It was approved in the US in February 2004 as a first-line treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer when administered in combination with standard chemotherapy. Subsequent studies have indicated that bevacizumab may have potential benefits in reducing tumor growth rates in patients with Neurofibromatosis Type 2, making it a candidate for therapeutic consideration in this context.
